layman_headline: Solana is surging toward our profit target — let the winner ride but tighten the safety net.
layman_explanation: Our Solana position is up 8.1% and closing in on the $115 profit target we set. The broader market is rallying with Bitcoin up 10% on the week, and major news like Morgan Stanley pushing Solana ETF inflows and Charles Schwab adding SOL to its platform are providing real institutional tailwinds. However, the market is getting greedy (Fear & Greed at 71) and most coins on the watchlist are already extended — this isn't the time to chase new entries.
layman_action: Hold the current Solana position and raise the stop-loss to $100 to lock in breakeven at minimum. Wait for the $115 target or signs of exhaustion before acting. Don't chase any of the extended altcoins right now.
expert_reasoning: SOL is already in our portfolio at $101.03 with 8.1% unrealized gain, approaching the $115 exit target. The 13% daily move on heavy volume ($7.4B) is driven by concrete institutional catalysts: Morgan Stanley-led ETF inflows and Charles Schwab platform integration. BTC's 10.4% weekly gain provides macro support. However, the 25.5% 7-day move means SOL is likely extended short-term, and Fear & Greed at 71 (trending toward greed) suggests caution on new entries. All swing candidates are either stablecoins, overbought (PUMP RSI 84), or have already run 30-40%+ in a week with no pullback. The prudent move is to raise the stop-loss to $100 (protecting ~breakeven) and let the position run toward $115. No new entry offers a favorable risk/reward ratio at this moment.
risk_factors: SOL has moved 25.5% in 7 days — a sharp pullback to the $95-100 range is likely if BTC stalls near $80K resistance
Fear & Greed at 71 and worsening — historically a 56% win rate signal, meaning nearly half of trades entered in greed conditions fail
BTC dominance at 59.2% means capital is concentrating in Bitcoin, which could starve altcoin rallies if BTC consolidates
watch_list: SOL price action near $115 resistance — take profit if momentum stalls or volume drops
BTC behavior at $80K — a rejection here could trigger a broad alt selloff
Whether SOL pulls back to $100-105 range, which would offer a potential re-entry or add opportunity
market_context: The crypto market is in a strong rally with BTC up 10.4% on the week driven by dollar weakness and $7B flowing into BTC/gold. Greed is rising (71) and most alts are extended — this favors holding winners rather than chasing new entries.
context_banner: Market is rallying hard but most altcoins are already extended — protect gains on the SOL position and wait for pullbacks before deploying new capital.

key_signals.description: Morgan Stanley leading $9M Solana ETF inflows as SOL crosses $100 — institutional demand catalyst supporting continued upside for our position.
Charles Schwab adding Solana to its crypto platform broadens retail and institutional access, a structural demand driver.
Fear & Greed at 71 (Greed) and worsening trend — historically only 56% win rate, cautioning against new entries in extended conditions.
SOL trading $7.4B daily volume with a 13% single-day move, confirming strong participation behind the rally rather than thin-market drift.
$7 billion flowing into Bitcoin and gold in five days as investors flee dollar weakness — macro tailwind supporting the entire crypto rally.
